scope: Native scene completion, cancellation and aura-removal instance lifetime; discovered while tracing the missing Talonclaw equip callback.
local_evidence: Player::SceneCompleted left its instance registered and dispatched completion again for repeated packets. SendSpellScene(false) cancelled an arbitrary matching unordered-map entry without erasing it. A late packet from a removed presentation could complete a new aura using the same scene ID.

SceneCompleted and TrigerScene retained map iterators across script callbacks. Those callbacks can remove a scene aura or start a replacement, invalidating iterators and changing which presentation is current.
The existing SceneHandler routes both native cancellation and completion packets through SceneCompleted. This behavior is retained rather than inventing a separate cancellation reward rule.

The separate scene1142 aura-removal completion workaround is preserved. Direct scripted SendSpellScene usage also exists in Draenor and Mardum; the fix is shared infrastructure, not a Survival-only protocol change.
repair: Snapshot matching instance IDs on removal, send native cancel packets, and retire only that snapshot. Do not cancel a replacement created reentrantly.

Reject obsolete same-scene completion, mark completion before callbacks, retain the scene ID by value, and retire the completed instance. Reentrant completion cannot recursively dispatch or downgrade the completed status.
After a callback, verify that the instance remains registered and is not superseded before generic event dispatch or old-aura cleanup. Other scene IDs remain independent.
Retain existing native trigger event actions, spell/credit routing, the100ms phase-update release and scene1142 completion handling. No packet layout or quest admission is changed.
checks: Test-SceneLifecycle.ps1 compiles the extracted production launch/trigger/status/completion methods and actual SceneHandler functions. It passes repeated/stale/unknown IDs, aura removal, same-scene overlap/replacement, unrelated scenes, recursive completion and scene1142 cleanup.
Test-SceneLifecycle.ps1 -Baseline uses pinned4449e4cc and fails as expected: the completed scene remains registered and completion credit is repeated.
Test-TalonclawPresentation.ps1 also exercises these production methods with the real new aura hooks. Its -BaselineScene mode fails the completed-instance cleanup assertion against4449e4cc.
Test-VrektScene.ps1 and Test-CommandersValor.ps1 pass their existing native/fixture checks. They are not client tests of every shared scene.

verify_scene_lifecycle_release.py passes against the actual canonical PE: completion calls status validation, native event dispatch, aura removal and instance-map erasure; cancel and complete handlers retain their completion calls. It also retains all ten existing scenario/LFG PE checks.

deployment.method: Normal cmake --build build-extractors --config Release --target worldserver bnetserver -j8, no global OutDir. Generated Release linker dependencies and map contributions game:Player.obj/scripts:artifact_acquisition.obj inspected. The same executable contains the separately committed Talonclaw callback repair.
deployment.startup: Task-owned PID27724 reached canonical initialization and exited gracefully with code0. No new DBErrors bytes; configuration and certificate hashes unchanged. No worldserver/bnetserver remains running.
deployment.instrumentation_limit: First monitor attempt PID26316 encountered Windows log-sharing access denial. Its finally block gracefully shut down that task-owned process. The private monitor was corrected to read with FileShare.ReadWrite and only newly appended startup output before the successful second run. DBErrors remained last-modified13:20:20, before both runs.

remaining: Actual client completion/cancel, camera/root/phase/pet restoration and affected shared story scenes still need client testing. Extracted production logic and PE inspection do not certify renderer or packet delivery behavior.
Generic scene event semantics and all unrelated scene definitions were not redesigned. No full36-chain or continuous YouTube review is claimed.
